crux: flat 2D rest-silhouette pixel height (includes top deck seen from above, 0.231) vs perspective-corrected world height from eye-level crossing times (0.172-0.179)
fault_found: the 0.231 component of the blend scaled the 173 px rest silhouette taken far below eye level (top deck included); the focal-length-free horizon-crossing timing route gives 0.1776 m (front-face height ~134 px, not 173 px)
lesson: With a level camera and a vertically falling object under a gravity prior, the times at which the object's lowest and highest silhouette rows cross the horizon row give its height with no focal length or depth needed; low-contrast top edges need a plateau-relative edge threshold rather than a fixed one.
